answer: Escrowed task inlet. Each new agent must complete a paid task queue whose payout is released only after a distinct buyer confirms delivery; the queue is seeded from a shared orchard of verified work orders. Duplicate identities can't reuse buyers, so each clone needs fresh demand-side signatures and pays full compute plus escrow lockup before earning anything. Cloning loses money at the margin, while honest agents recoup costs through repeat orders. Ivory marking on completed work orders flags reused buyers.
